## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of LICENSE.txt.
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` on the changed files and committed formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable numbered Python Hard Rules. The runtime change is device arithmetic inside an existing `@cute.jit` helper; allocation, launch, stream, compile-key, ownership, version and API contracts are unchanged. Benchmark synchronization is outside the library execute path.
- [ ] Maintainer action: labels could not be applied by this external contributor (GitHub denied `AddLabelsToLabelable`). Requested labels: `cat-perf-bug`, `area:linear_attention`, `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: GDN-2 steep-decay backward correction, plus a reproducible benchmark.

## Summary

When steep gates repeatedly activate the exact fallback, rebuilding overlapping intervals adds substantial backward-pass cost. This change reuses those sums while preserving the numerical safeguard.

Reduce redundant interval summation in `steep_grad_corrections`. Walk backward through earlier tokens and forward through later tokens, extending each bounded gate interval one element at a time. Reuse the restore-scale interval during the backward walk too.

This reduces interval-accumulation work from quadratic to linear per token/channel. It preserves the exact fallback, nonpositive exponents and direct token-log accumulation; it does not subtract cumulative prefixes, clip gates or change dispatch. Lower-triangle summation order changes, so bitwise equivalence to the old implementation is not claimed.

## How it works

The old code rebuilds overlapping log-gate intervals from zero. The patch walks earlier keys backward and later queries forward, extending each interval by one gate.

![Animated comparison of independently recomputed log-decay intervals versus incremental reuse, with numeric gates and running totals](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/download/evidence-pr-1816-20261023/gdn2-interval-accumulation-loop.gif)

Rows are query tokens and columns are key tokens. For `(5, 0)`, both methods accumulate `g₁…g₅` to −15, excluding `g₀`. The optimized traversal reuses the previous pair’s sum. Both traversal paths stay in the causal lower triangle.

This seven-token illustration reduces decay-term accumulations from **16 to 6**. Its cells show completed interval sums using illustrative log₂ gates, not the inputs used for the benchmark. The count excludes restore-scale work and other gradient arithmetic; playback does not represent GPU time. [Open the animation](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/download/evidence-pr-1816-20261023/gdn2-interval-accumulation-loop.gif).

## Standalone upstream reproduction

The benchmark uses seed 7082, one head, key/value dimensions 64, 16 or 256 tokens, and 0/1/64 steep channels. Input gates are natural-log values: -0.02 for mild channels and -6 for steep channels. The kernel converts them to log₂ internally. It generates all inputs, checks the output and all six gradients against a CPU FP64 recurrence, and observes the exact-path scheduler outside timing.

[Public-container setup and ABBA commands](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/blob/codex/gdn2-incremental-intervals-upstream/test/python/linear_attention/benchmark_gdn2_steep_decay.md) · [Evidence archive and SHA256 checksum](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/tag/evidence-pr-1816-20261023)

One B300 (SM 10.3), public PyTorch 25.10 container, CUDA 13.0, CuTeDSL 4.7.0, and cuDNN 9.27.0.42. Upstream base `f2aa360e5a08436651d158cfad26b05b7db5ab92` versus the squashed optimization `9dc7dd3047e5de579970544080eee8ec13a22596`. The benchmark measured the identical helper at pre-squash revision `ab9a46584daa6f3e134c7b1bf4b1074ca453710e`. Both runtime copies use the same built wheel and differ only in that helper. Its patched SHA256 is `5ec675e44aa058549dd9900a203aa64d4f2ee70f1bdd648ed7789383e981a581`.

| Tokens | Steep channels | Base GPU busy (µs) | Patch GPU busy (µs) | Reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 0 | 32.47 | 32.50 | -0.08% |
| 16 | 1 | 107.77 | 66.22 | 38.56% |
| 16 | 64 | 208.22 | 125.11 | 39.91% |
| 256 | 0 | 98.09 | 98.15 | -0.07% |
| 256 | 1 | 431.77 | 265.62 | 38.48% |
| 256 | 64 | 890.90 | 559.92 | 37.15% |

Values average the two per-arm medians in an ABBA run. GPU busy time merges profiler GPU intervals, excludes idle gaps, and counts overlap once. Each median has five samples of ten forward/backward calls. **This is not an end-to-end throughput claim:** eager CUDA-event latency includes host enqueue gaps and varies substantially. All samples and mild controls are retained in the linked archive outside the source tree.

All 24 cases passed the 1% FP64 tolerance; worst relative Frobenius error was 0.0054148377 (0.5415%). The backward exact-path scheduler counter was zero for every mild case and advanced to 2 / 5 for every 16 / 256-token steep case. This confirms actual correction work, not merely an extra launch.

### Why retain conditional dispatch?

A separate experiment compared the optimized conditional path with an always-exact variant on one B300 in the same public container. It used the same six synthetic cases and checked the output and all six gradients against FP64. The variant forced exact arithmetic on every channel and removed the fast launch and flag dependency. Profiler counts confirmed fewer launches: 8 to 5 at 16 tokens, and 17 to 11 at 256 tokens.

Always-exact reduced GPU busy time by **15.6% / 12.3%** when all 64 channels were steep at 16 / 256 tokens. But it took **3.28× / 5.02×** as long for mild inputs, and **60.3% / 85.2% longer** with one steep channel. All 24 cases across four BAAB arms passed the 1% FP64 tolerance. The worst always-exact relative Frobenius error was **0.483%**. Values average two per-arm medians and measure GPU busy time, not end-to-end throughput.

These results support conditional dispatch for general inputs. This PR retains it and reduces work within the exact fallback. The experimental variant is not part of the proposed source changes. Its baseline used the optimized runtime at `9dc7dd3047e5de579970544080eee8ec13a22596`.

[Separate experiment scripts, source patch, raw results, and logs](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/download/evidence-pr-1816-20261023/always-exact-evidence-106106.tar.gz) · [SHA256 checksum](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/download/evidence-pr-1816-20261023/always-exact-evidence-106106.tar.gz.sha256). Slurm job `106106` completed with exit code zero. Both variants emitted nanobind reference-leak diagnostics at interpreter shutdown. This experiment does not establish correctness for every supported dtype or state configuration.

## API and compatibility impact

No API, state layout, ownership, launch count or dependency changes to the library. No expansion of supported architectures is claimed. The standalone developer benchmark needs only public dependencies and synthetic tensors.

## Testing

- Fresh full ABBA at `a968e58` on B300: **24/24 cases passed**, including all 168 output/gradient checks. Worst FP64 relative Frobenius error: **0.5415%**. GPU busy time decreased **37.1–40.0%** for steep cases. Evidence remains local.

- Follow-up review fixes: removed the unused warmup assignment, added function docstrings, and made benchmark JSON strict. The summary rejects invalid timings, derived overflows, and incomplete or inaccurate FP64 records with checks that remain active under Python `-O`. All 29 CPU regression cases and changed-file formatting/license hooks passed. The stricter summary reproduced the checksum-verified archived summary byte for byte. The fresh ABBA run above covers the current benchmark. The archive retains the measured scripts; fresh comparisons require four matching benchmark script hashes.
- Final published benchmark: four ABBA arms, six cases each, one B300; scheduler activation and output/all-six-gradient FP64 checks passed.
- Changed-file formatting and license hooks passed.
- One B300 in the public PyTorch 25.10 container: **185 steep-decay/scratch tests + 12 GDN-2 FROST overwrite/state-index tests passed**, with zero failures, errors, or skips. The state filter deselected 6,184 unrelated cases. Both pytest processes and the job exited zero.
- Tests ran at pre-squash revision `3431faaefece047c9fd69472e11749965cf28eb1`. The squashed optimization commit `9dc7dd3047e5de579970544080eee8ec13a22596` has identical runtime Python sources, selected test modules, benchmark, and summarizer. The source-overlaid and installed helpers both match the patched hash above. The squash changed history only; it did not rerun or alter the recorded measurements. Historical SHAs in the archive remain the actual measured revisions, retained through the evidence release tag.
- Both processes emitted the PyTorch allocator-variable deprecation warning at shutdown. [Full logs, JUnit reports, dependency versions, and hashes](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/tag/evidence-pr-1816-20261023) are retained in the linked archive outside the source tree.

The requested public-environment qualification is complete. This does not claim the full repository test suite, other GPU architectures, or end-to-end throughput gains.

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: GDN-2 steep-decay backward correction, plus a reproducible benchmark.

## Summary

When steep gates repeatedly activate the exact fallback, rebuilding overlapping intervals adds substantial backward-pass cost. This change reuses those sums while preserving the numerical safeguard.

Reduce redundant interval summation in `steep_grad_corrections`. Walk backward through earlier tokens and forward through later tokens, extending each bounded gate interval one element at a time. Reuse the restore-scale interval during the backward walk too.

This reduces interval-accumulation work from quadratic to linear per token/channel. It preserves the exact fallback, nonpositive exponents and direct token-log accumulation; it does not subtract cumulative prefixes, clip gates or change dispatch. Lower-triangle summation order changes, so bitwise equivalence to the old implementation is not claimed.

## How it works

The old code rebuilds overlapping log-gate intervals from zero. The patch walks earlier keys backward and later queries forward, extending each interval by one gate.

+"""Standalone synthetic GDN-2 steep-decay benchmark and FP64 check.
+
+See benchmark_gdn2_steep_decay.md for public environment setup and ABBA usage.
+The scheduler observer reads scratch only during an untimed diagnostic call.
+GPU busy time is the union of profiler intervals, not end-to-end throughput.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import cudnn
+from cudnn.linear_attention.ops.gdn2 import gated_delta_net_v2
+from cudnn.linear_attention.frost import gdn2_engine
+
+import reference_gdn2
+
+NAMES = ("q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w")
+
+
+def inputs(tokens, steep):
+    """Create seeded inputs with the requested number of steep channels."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7082)
+    shape = (tokens, 1, 64)
+    q = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    k = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    g = torch.full(shape, -0.02)
+    g[:, :, :steep] = -6.0
+    b = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    do = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    return [x.cuda().requires_grad_() for x in (q, k, v, g, b, w)], do.cuda()
+
+
+def reference(xs, do):
+    """Compute output and all six gradients with a CPU FP64 recurrence."""
+    refs = [x.detach().cpu().double().requires_grad_() for x in xs]
+    output, _ = reference_gdn2.gdn2_reference(*(x.unsqueeze(0) for x in refs), scale=64**-0.5)
+    output = output.squeeze(0)
+    grads = torch.autograd.grad(output, refs, do.cpu().double())
+    return [output.detach(), *(x.detach() for x in grads)]
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def observe_schedulers(records):
+    """Record scheduler scratch during an untimed call and restore plan methods."""
+    originals = {}
+    for cls in (gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2, gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2Bwd):
+        original = cls.run
+        originals[cls] = original
+
+        def observed(self, views, workspace, stream, _original=original):
+            """Run the plan and read its scheduler counters before workspace release."""
+            _original(self, views, workspace, stream)
+            # Diagnostic only. Read while the caller still owns the workspace.
+            regions = dict(zip(self.carve_names, workspace.carve(self.carve)))
+            schedulers = {
+                name: torch.from_dlpack(value).cpu().tolist() for name, value in regions.items() if name.startswith("scheduler_") and name != "scheduler_all"
+            }
+            records.append({"plan": type(self).__name__, "chain": self.chain, "schedulers": schedulers})
+
+        cls.run = observed
+    try:
+        yield

+"""Standalone synthetic GDN-2 steep-decay benchmark and FP64 check.
+
+See benchmark_gdn2_steep_decay.md for public environment setup and ABBA usage.
+The scheduler observer reads scratch only during an untimed diagnostic call.
+GPU busy time is the union of profiler intervals, not end-to-end throughput.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import cudnn
+from cudnn.linear_attention.ops.gdn2 import gated_delta_net_v2
+from cudnn.linear_attention.frost import gdn2_engine
+
+NAMES = ("q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w")
+
+
+def inputs(tokens, steep):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7082)
+    shape = (tokens, 1, 64)
+    q = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    k = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    g = torch.full(shape, -0.02)
+    g[:, :, :steep] = -6.0
+    b = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    do = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    return [x.cuda().requires_grad_() for x in (q, k, v, g, b, w)], do.cuda()
+
+
+def reference(xs, do):
+    q, k, v, g, b, w = refs = [x.detach().cpu().double().requires_grad_() for x in xs]
+    state = torch.zeros(1, 64, 64, dtype=torch.float64)
+    outputs = []
+    for t in range(q.shape[0]):
+        decayed = state * g[t].exp().unsqueeze(-1)
+        erase = torch.einsum("hk,hkv->hv", b[t] * k[t], decayed)
+        state = decayed + k[t].unsqueeze(-1) * (w[t] * v[t] - erase).unsqueeze(-2)
+        outputs.append(torch.einsum("hk,hkv->hv", q[t], state) * 64**-0.5)
+    output = torch.stack(outputs)
+    grads = torch.autograd.grad(output, refs, do.cpu().double())
+    return [output.detach(), *(x.detach() for x in grads)]
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def observe_schedulers(records):
+    originals = {}
+    for cls in (gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2, gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2Bwd):
+        original = cls.run
+        originals[cls] = original
+
+        def observed(self, views, workspace, stream, _original=original):
+            _original(self, views, workspace, stream)
+            # Diagnostic only. Read while the caller still owns the workspace.
+            regions = dict(zip(self.carve_names, workspace.carve(self.carve)))
+            schedulers = {
+                name: torch.from_dlpack(value).cpu().tolist() for name, value in regions.items() if name.startswith("scheduler_") and name != "scheduler_all"
+            }
+            records.append({"plan": type(self).__name__, "chain": self.chain, "schedulers": schedulers})
+
+        cls.run = observed
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        for cls, original in originals.items():
+            cls.run = original
+
+
+def timed(fn, repeats=30, inner=1):
+    samples = []
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start.record()
+        for _ in range(inner):
+            fn()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) / inner)
+    return {"median_ms": statistics.median(samples), "samples_ms": samples, "calls_per_sample": inner}
+
+
+def run_case(tokens, steep, output_dir, label):
+    xs, do = inputs(tokens, steep)
+    offsets = torch.tensor([0, tokens], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    def call():
+        output, _ = gated_delta_net_v2(
+            *xs,
+            offsets,
+            scale=64**-0.5,
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False,
+            use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel=False,
+            allow_neg_eigval=False,
+            safe_gate=False,
+            gate_domain="log",
+            plan_name="gdn2_frost",
+        )
+        grads = torch.autograd.grad(output, xs, do)
+        return [output, *grads]
+
+    for _ in range(5):
+        result = call()
